_comment: The emulator hotkeys: which actions exist, and what they're bound to out of the box. Parsed by ShortcutRegistry (libs/firelight/input); the app passes the path. Adding an action here is all it takes for it to appear in the shortcut editor â€” but nothing will happen until something dispatches it, so add a handler too.
_activation: 'press' fires once on the rising edge. 'hold' fires again on release, which is what makes hold-to-fast-forward work. There is no 'toggle': an action like pause flips state that is global to the emulator, and the engine only ever sees one device, so it reports the edge and the handler owns the value.
_scope: 'in-game', 'in-menu', or 'always'. The engine only fires an action whose scope includes the current context.
_bindings: A binding is a name, or names joined with '+' where everything before the last one must be held: 'Select+R3'. Gamepad names are the GamepadInput enum (include/firelight/input/gamepad_input.hpp); keyboard names are Qt::Key values ('Key_F1'), resolved through Qt's meta-object system. Each action takes a list, in preference order: seeding keeps the ones the controller actually has, so a pad with no R3 falls through to the next.
_combos: Pad bindings are combos on purpose. When a shortcut fires, its trigger input is withheld from the game â€” which is only safe if the combo can tell the two intents apart. Bind a bare button and that button stops reaching the game entirely while in-game.
_no_rewind: There is deliberately no 'rewind' action. Rewinding here is ten snapshots taken every few seconds and picked from a menu (open_rewind_menu), not the frame-by-frame history a hold-to-rewind needs â€” so declaring one would put a key in the editor that could never do anything. Add it when there's an engine behind it.

actions.label: Turn hotkeys off
actions._note: The one action that still works while hotkeys are off â€” otherwise there'd be no way back. Turning them off hands every input straight to the game, which is what a core that wants the whole keyboard (DOS, Amiga, MSX, ScummVM) needs. Affects only the device that pressed it, so a second pad keeps its hotkeys.

presets.label: Firelight
presets._note: Select is the modifier: no core reads it during play as often as the face buttons, and every pad has one. Guide/Home is deliberately unbound â€” Steam claims it globally and we can't stop it.

presets.label: RetroArch (keyboard)
presets._note: RetroArch's own shipped keyboard defaults, for people arriving from it. RetroArch ships no gamepad defaults at all â€” the SELECT+ layout people associate with it comes from handheld distros, so it lives under 'handheld' below rather than being passed off as RetroArch's.
presets._omitted: RetroArch's rewind (R), slow motion (E) and reset (H) are missing on purpose: RetroArch binds no triggers or sticks on the keyboard, so those keys are free there â€” here they're the triggers and right stick. Binding them would fire the hotkey and press the button, and (once a shortcut withholds its trigger from the game) would cost the key for gameplay entirely. Rebind them yourself if you'd rather have the hotkey.

presets.label: Handheld (SELECT + button)
presets._note: The combo layout Batocera/RetroPie generate into retroarch.cfg. Familiar to anyone coming from a handheld distro.
